LESSON: SONGS

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMING
Topic 1.1: Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Songs. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify and name different types of songs performed for different purposes in the Kenyan folksongs, lullabies, patriotic community for awareness,
2. sing a variety of age appropriate songs in unison paying attention to accuracy in pitch and rhythm for enjoyment and self-expression,
3. sing all verses of the Kenya national anthem in English and/or Kiswahili with proper etiquette for patriotism, cohesion and peaceful coexistence,
4. sing 3-part rounds, keeping to the respective parts for enjoyment e) execute the elements of music while singing for effective communication, f) use vocal techniques in singing a variety of songs for effective communication, musicianship such as good posture, 340 Property of the Government of Kenya g) express ideas, feelings and emotions through singing for self-expression, h) perform songs individually and in groups for enjoyment i) sing songs with co- ordinated body movements for self-expression, discuss the importance of singing songs j) appreciate the importance of singing songs from diverse cultures and time, k) record own and others performances using electronic devices for appreciation and digital literacy. guided to record own and others performances using electronic devices

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Songs.
2. Explain Songs to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Songs.
4. Show that you can: identify and name different types of songs performed for different purposes in the Kenyan folksongs, lullabies, patriotic community for awareness,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Songs. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Songs important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
